Zarnowiec New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Żarnowiec, Poland

Not demolished. Żarnowiec's Jewish settlement dates to the 17th century, with an independent community likely already established by the 18th; the population peaked at 1,412 (57 percent) by 1897, before falling to 574 by 1938. This cemetery, most likely established in the 19th century and used until WWII, holds the postwar grave of Rabbi Ruwen ha-Lewi Horowic — son of Rabbi Jakow Chaim, grandson of a rabbi of Tykocin, documented elsewhere in this collection, author of the book 'Dudaim BaSade,' and a student of both Elimelech of Leżajsk and the Seer of Lublin. In February 1941, the Germans deported all of Żarnowiec's Jews to the Żarki Ghetto, documented elsewhere in this collection.
